surface_mechanism_description: The catalytic effect of vanadium(V) oxytriisopropoxide (VTIP) on the subsequent deposition from BiPh3 enables the first ALD of bismuth vanadates. The deposition of BiPh3 is catalyzed by the V2O5 surface, leading to the formation of bismuth vanadates. The process involves the sequential exposure of the substrate to pulses of gas phase precursors, with the [VTIP–W–BiPh3–W] cycle resulting in the deposition of bismuth vanadates. The catalytic effect of VTIP on BiPh3 deposition is crucial for the formation of bismuth vanadates.
evidence: The catalytic effect of vanadium(V) oxytriisopropoxide (VTIP) on the subsequent deposition from BiPh3 enables the first ALD of bismuth vanadates. Post processing of these films led to phase-pure and photoactive BiVO4 with the scheelite crystal structure. The [VTIP–W–BiPh3–W] cycle was found to result in a reduced deposition rate of 0.07 /C138 per metal cycle compared to the [VTIP–W] cycle. The deposition of BiPh3 is catalyzed by the V2O5 surface, leading to the formation of bismuth vanadates.
